question:
Which of the following statements related to the men’s hockey competition at the 38th National Games 2025 are correct?

1) Karnataka defeated Uttar Pradesh by a one-goal margin in the final.

2) The semifinal between Karnataka and Maharashtra ended in a draw and was decided through a shootout.

3) Punjab secured the bronze medal by beating Maharashtra.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**1, 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **38th National Games** is a prominent event in India, showcasing athletic excellence in various sports.
 
• In the **men’s hockey competition**, **Karnataka defeated Uttar Pradesh** in the final by a close one-goal margin, highlighting a competitive and thrilling match.
 
• The **semifinal** between Karnataka and Maharashtra ended in a **draw**, and the winner was decided through a **shootout**, which is a common method in hockey for resolving tied matches.
 
• **Punjab secured the bronze medal** by defeating Maharashtra, indicating a strong performance by Punjab in the third-place match.
 
• Hockey is a significant sport in India, and the National Games provide a platform for players to display their skills and gain recognition on a national level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **National Games** are held every four years in India, and they consist of multiple events across various sports disciplines.
 
• **Hockey** is one of the most anticipated sports during the National Games due to its historical and cultural significance in India.
 
• **Penalty shootouts** are often used in hockey when matches end in a draw to determine the winner in knockout stages, adding excitement and pressure to the game.
 
• The achievements of teams like **Karnataka**, **Punjab**, and **Uttar Pradesh** in the tournament reflect the growing competitiveness and talent pool in Indian hockey.
